svg.text: Appsec Advisor · 0.6.0b4 · 8 components · 18 data flows · 3 trust boundaries (2 inferred) · 60 threats
acts on the pipeline, not on traffic

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-01; tb-2 External → C-08; tb-4 C-01 → External

df-002: POST /rest/user/login with email and password; no CSRF protection observed (HTTP) df-003: POST /rest/user/login with OAuth implicit-flow access token extracted from URL fragment (HTTP) df-002 authentication: Email and password credentials submitted to /rest/user/login; evidence: routes/login.ts:18 df-002 access group: Login method; alternatives; step n/a df-003 authentication: OAuth access token received from URL fragment after provider redirect; RFC 9700 deprecates implicit flow; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:152 df-003 access group: Login method; alternatives; step n/a

df-004: POST /rest/2fa/verify submits TOTP code; conditional on account MFA enrollment (HTTP) df-004 authentication: TOTP one-time code submitted as second factor for enrolled accounts; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:16

df-005: POST /rest/user/reset-password with security question answer; no rate limiting evidenced (HTTP) df-005 authentication: Security question answer used to authorize password reset without email token; evidence: routes/resetPassword.ts:16

df-008: Unauthenticated REST API calls to /api/* and /rest/* endpoints; many lack auth check (HTTP) df-009: Authenticated REST API calls with Authorization: Bearer JWT; token stored in localStorage (XSS-accessible) (HTTP) df-008 authentication: Product catalog, user registration, feedback, and several management endpoints require no token; evidence: server.ts:197 df-008 access group: API access variant; alternatives; step n/a df-009 authentication: JWT bearer token stored in localStorage, injected by request.interceptor.ts on every outbound request; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:158, frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:13 df-009 access group: API access variant; alternatives; step n/a

df-010: Auth routes query SQLite user table for credential verification, 2FA state, and session tracking via Sequelize ORM (sqlite) df-010 authentication: In-process Sequelize call to file-based SQLite; no network authentication required; evidence: routes/login.ts:18

df-011: Application routes query and mutate SQLite tables for baskets, orders, products, addresses, and payment cards (sqlite) df-011 authentication: In-process Sequelize ORM call to local SQLite file; no network authentication; evidence: server.ts:603

df-012: Product-review routes read and write marsdb document collection via in-process API (in-process) df-012 authentication: In-process marsdb API; no network authentication; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-013: Angular SPA opens Socket.IO WebSocket connection for real-time notifications; no token required (WebSocket) df-013 authentication: Socket.IO handshake carries no authentication credential; any visitor can connect; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/socket-io.service.ts:8

df-014: Server pushes challenge-solved events and scoreboard updates over Socket.IO to all connected browser clients (WebSocket) df-014 authentication: Events broadcast to all connected clients; no per-recipient authentication; evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:20

df-015: POST /rest/chat proxies user message to OpenAI-compatible LLM API; endpoint reachable without authentication (HTTPS) df-015 authentication: API key authenticates backend to LLM service; incoming /rest/chat route carries no caller authentication; evidence: routes/chat.ts:221

df-016: POST /file-upload accepts multipart file uploads from unauthenticated callers; intentional vulnerability surface (HTTP) df-017: GET /metrics exposes Prometheus metrics without authentication; reveals application internals and version info (HTTP) df-016 authentication: File upload endpoint has no authentication check; any unauthenticated actor can upload arbitrary files; evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:19 df-017 authentication: Production metrics route registered in server.ts lacks authentication; challenge codefixes demonstrate auth variants; evidence: routes/metrics.ts:45
df-018: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:48, frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:81
Internet Attacker → C-01 · Backend Express API: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6; its findings also affect C-04 · SQLite Relational Datastore, C-07 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Authentication & Session Surface: scenario 1, 2, 4; its findings also affect C-01 · Backend Express API
Internet Attacker → C-07 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 2, 3, 4
Internet Attacker → C-06 · Socket.IO Real-Time Channel: scenario 4
Internet Attacker → Appsec Advisor User: scenario 6, 7
Supply-Chain / Build Attacker → C-08 · CI/CD Pipeline & Container Build: scenario 8
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:61 (reported finding)

Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:83 (reported finding); Server-side templates — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:87 (reported finding); Payment processing — evidence: server.ts:440
C-01 · Backend Express API: Application Configuration and Internals
C-03 · Angular SPA Client: Session JWT Tokens
C-04 · SQLite Relational Datastore: User Account Credentials
C-04 · SQLite Relational Datastore: User Personal Data (PII)
C-04 · SQLite Relational Datastore: Payment Card Data
C-04 · SQLite Relational Datastore: Product Catalog
C-04 · SQLite Relational Datastore: Challenge Progress and Scoreboard Data
C-05 · marsdb Embedded Document Store: Product Catalog
Unauthenticated internet user accessing the application via a web browser. Includes security trainees and potential attackers reaching public endpoints.
External OAuth 2.0 authorization server used for social login. The SPA performs an implicit-flow redirect; token is returned in the URL fragment to the browser.
Remote large-language-model inference endpoint (OpenAI-compatible or Ollama local). Called from POST /rest/chat; also used by validatePreconditions.ts to verify model availability at startup.
Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

External OAuth Identity Provider df-006: Browser redirected to OAuth provider authorization endpoint for implicit-flow grant (HTTP); Client-initiated OAuth implicit-flow redirect to external identity provider df-007: OAuth provider redirects browser to SPA with access token in URL fragment (implicit flow callback) (HTTP); Completes the sign-in: the provider returns its result to the client's registered redirect URI

C-03 · Angular SPA Client df-006: Browser redirected to OAuth provider authorization endpoint for implicit-flow grant (HTTP); Client-initiated OAuth implicit-flow redirect to external identity provider df-007: OAuth provider redirects browser to SPA with access token in URL fragment (implicit flow callback) (HTTP); Completes the sign-in: the provider returns its result to the client's registered redirect URI

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
User input reaches server-side eval functions
Stored XSS steals active user sessions
OAuth CSRF links accounts without consent
Compromise the Build or Its Inputs
The recipient performs no authentication check on this connection.
The recipient checks the supplied password.
The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.
The caller presents a configured service credential.
Delegated access; only the evidenced protocol step is covered.
Security question answer used to authorize password reset without
TOTP one-time code submitted as second factor for enrolled accounts
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
